result_text:
I changed `exportJson` in `DataExporter.java` so `all_files.zip` now takes its entry names from the configured aspect names. The `reports` module compiles and the `DataExport*` tests pass. I did not run an export with a renamed aspect, so the rename case is untested.

The method used to hard-code `aspect_main.txt` through `aspect_other.txt`, including `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`. After a rename, the hard-coded `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` was never written, so reading it threw. That exception skipped `all_files.zip` and `git-history.zip`.

It now collects the five scope aspects in the same order and calls `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")` for each. That helper is the one the loose-file writer uses, so the names match what was written. The same name is used to read each file and to label its zip entry.

With the default configuration the entries and their order are unchanged. With the renamed aspect, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`, and `git-history.zip` is written when a `git-history.txt` exists.

I left `LandscapeAnalyzer.java` alone, though it also hard-codes the scope file names (lines 280–284). It wasn't part of this task.
